videos.caption: "LAZY GIRL" CHICKEN THIGHS✨ use this foolproof technique for tender and juicy chicken thighs every time! Whenever a recipe calls for cooked chicken, 90% of the time this is how I'm going to prepare it. No oil, 2 ingredients (four if we count S&P but I don't think those count), under 30 minutes. You're going to LOVE this recipe! Recipe below or you can find it on my blog at the link in my bio Ingredients:  1 1/2 lbs of chicken thighs, boneless and skinless salt and pepper to season (about 1/4 tsp salt per thigh, and 1/8 tsp pepper) about 1/2 cup of low sodium chicken broth or bone broth Directions:  Heat a large cast iron skillet over medium high heat While the skillet heats up, season the chicken thighs generously on both sides with salt and pepper  Add the chicken thighs to the dry skillet, making sure not to overcrowd the pan, and cook, undisturbed, for 10-12 minutes or until they are white around the edges and are no longer sticking to the pan. It's important not to move them around while cooking because you want a nice golden crust to form.  Flip the chicken once it can easily release from the pan and cook for another 5-7 minutes. Lower the pan heat to medium low and add 1/4 cup of chicken broth, scraping up any chicken bits as the broth deglazes the pan, then add another 1/4 cup to cover the bottom on the pan in a thin layer. Allow the sauce to reduce until there is only a thin, sticky glaze over the bottom of the pan, tossing the chicken in the sauce as you go, for another 3-5 minutes. Remove the chicken from the skillet and allow to rest for 5 minutes before slicing.  Slice into your juicy chicken thighs, serve (with the pan drippings), and ENJOY! The tips and tricks to making the PERFECT chicken cutlets every time 🔥 There are few things in life better than a beautiful, thin, crispy yet still juicy chicken cutlet. It’s something I grew up on and can probably eat everyday. While my Nonna equipped me with the recipe to make some pretty great cutlets, culinary school taught me the reasons and techniques of WHY and HOW to do it. So here is all the info ~ Tips & tricks:  🔪 Butterfly your chicken breast. Place one hand on top of the breast flat and using a shape knife, begin making long straight motions* into the side of the breast. With each cut, open it up like a book and once you’ve made it to the end flatten it out and slice in half. *It’s important to avoid a saw motion to keep the slices as even and clean as possible.  🔪 Pound it out! For an even and thin cutlet, use a meat mallet or any heavy object with a flat surface and begin pounding out the cutlet. Start in the center and work your way to the edges.  🔪Set up the dredging station. FLOUR, EGG, BREADCRUMB… that is the name of the game. Get them in plates or trays right next to each other and season EACH one to maximize and layer the flavor. Feel free to have fun and add more spices and seasonings. I love adding parmigiano and parsley to the breadcrumb for added flavor or even orange and lemon zest in the summer!!  🔪 Shallow fry the cutlets. Pick your favorite frying oil (mine is olive oil for cutlets as it adds in a really nice subtle flavor) and add it to a pan so that it’ll reach 1/2 way up the cutlet ~ not submerging it. Allow it to heat up of medium LOW heat, because you want it to get golden while cooking the chicken. Cook until golden brown on both sides.  🔪Remove from the oil and season immediately. While the oil is still hot, hit the chicken with salt so that it can be absorbed into the chicken.  . . . #Chickencutlets #chickenrecipe #culinaryschool #learntocook

How I make perfectly crispy & juicy chicken THIGHLETS 🔥 There are few things in life better than a beautiful, crisp, and juicy chicken THIGHLET. It’s something I can probably eat every day. The simple swap of chicken thighs over chicken breast yields in my opinion the best cutlet in the world. Below, you can find the tips and tricks on how to make it.  Tips & tricks: 🔪 Use BONELESS & SKINLESS chicken THIGHS. Don’t be afraid of dark meat as that is the KEY to making these cutlets ultra juicy!! 🔪 Pounding it out…. To me, this is optional as I like to keep a little thickness on it, but if you prefer it thinner, use a meat mallet or any heavy object with a flat surface and begin pounding out the cutlet. Start in the center and work your way to the edges. 🔪Set up the dredging station. FLOUR, EGG, PANKO BREADCRUMB… that is the name of the game. Get them in plates or trays right next to each other and season EACH one to maximize and layer the flavor. Feel free to have fun and add more spices and seasonings. I love adding Parmigiano to the breadcrumb for added flavor or even orange and lemon zest in the summer!! 🔪 Shallow fry the cutlets. Pick your favorite frying oil (mine is olive oil for cutlets as it adds in a really nice subtle flavor) and add it to a pan so that it’ll reach 1/2 way up the cutlet ~ not submerging it. Allow it to heat up on medium heat because you want it to get golden while cooking the chicken. Cook until golden brown on both sides. 🔪Remove from the oil and season immediately.
